utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Dupud, you've given already a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Hedaraly will now put further questions to you. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovan Dupud.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Dupud, are you appearing here today to testify voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I came because I received a subpoena from the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have 65 ter number 4826 [sic] on the screen, please. That's the statement of the witness, if I could provide him with a hard copy in his language.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, do you recall being interviewed by representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on 21 and 22 February, 2008 [sic] and providing a written statement to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Hedaraly, it is 2007, I believe is the statement date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. And the 65 ter number should be 4829.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question again. Do you remember giving a statement on the 21 and 22 February 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you look on the screen on the computer in front of you, is that the statement that you gave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to review the statement before today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we're looking at statements on the screen. If we could look at them always including signatures, which we all know appear on the bottom of the page but are not visible on the screen. The English, yes, there we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you reviewed your statement, you informed us of two minor corrections. I will just run through them with you and you can confirm that these are indeed corrections to be made to your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I said that two things should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The first one was in paragraph 1 in the last line, when it says: "I was asked to be released from military duties," it should say: "I asked to be released from military duties." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in paragraph 4, page 3 of the statement, in the English version, there's a sentence that says: "A larger second group left starting at about midnight towards villages around Obrovac," and that should be "a larger second group left starting at about midnight from villages around Obrovac." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around Obrovac, yes. It says here "the second larger group started leaving around midnight towards the villages around Obrovac," but it should say, "the second larger group left off from the villages around Obrovac towards Serbia around 8.00."

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. And with these two corrections, does your statement accurately reflect what you said to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the contents of that statement that you signed in February 2007, subject to those two corrections, are true to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today that you were asked in February last year, would you give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would like to have 65 ter 4829 be admitted into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With the additional clarification of the spelling of the witness's name, we have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then it is on the record now that the name of the witness is spelled not Dupud but Dupud, D-o-p-u-d, but then pronounced in the way Dopudj. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P548.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P548 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to read out a short summary of the evidence of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud was born in the Obrovac municipality and lived there all his life until Operation Storm. He witnessed the shelling of Obrovac on several occasions prior to Operation Storm. On the 4th of August, 1995, he observed the shelling of civilian objects in the town of Obrovac such as a cafe/restaurant in the centre of town, a health clinic, and a movie theatre. He also witnessed the shelling of surrounding villages such as Krusevo, Bilisane, Zelengrad, Zaton, Muskovici, Bogatnik, and Zegar. Mr. Dupud also provides evidence regarding the departure of the Serb civilian population from the town of Obrovac in the morning of 4 August 1995 and the departure of Serb civilians from the surrounding area towards Serbia. He also provides information that he heard about the killing of approximately eight people, most of them elderly civilians, from the village of Zegar. Mr. Dupud also provides evidence about crimes committed by members of the Croatian army during military operations that occurred in June 1992 in Miljevac Plateau and in January 1993 in Maslenica. This concludes my summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, I want to ask you some questions to clarify some of the contents of your statement that has now been admitted into evidence. First of all, in paragraph 3 of your statement, you said that the population started leaving the town of Obrovac when the shelling started. Can you please tell us what time that was, approximately, that the people started leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shelling of the area surrounding Obrovac began early in the morning, around 5.00. The shelling of the -- of Obrovac town itself began around 7.00. It lasted -- it was very short, but sufficient for the population that had remained in Obrovac because a large majority had houses in villages. In other words, the people who were in Obrovac, they left Obrovac. The evacuation, or, rather, the leaving of Obrovac was not a planned event. It wasn't a planned evacuation. People left Obrovac any way they could, on their own or on buses, which began around 8.30 an ended around 10.30. Already at 10.30, there were no civilians in Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm just trying to parse through your answer. I asked you about what time the civilians start leaving. So are you saying that that would be before 10.30?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from Obrovac itself. In other words, immediately after the shelling stopped, the shelling of Obrovac town, and in this group my wife and children left so that I really recall this vividly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me turn to paragraph 5 of your statement where you refer to some individuals that were killed from the village of Zegar. One of these you identified as with the last name Macura and between 65 and 70 years old. Do you remember his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Nedeljko Macura, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the Chamber's information this person is on the list of additional killings and we're preparing a bar table motion for all the documentation linked to those killings that we will try to file shortly. This witness does not have any other evidence of that so I won't ask him anymore questions, but just so that the Chamber is aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll wait until that request or that motion is filed and then we hear from the Defence, I will take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether there is any objection against it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just two points so I can make my record here, Your Honour. The remaining individuals identified in paragraph 5 are not on the Prosecution's either schedule in the indictment or on the additional killings which I think Mr. Hedaraly and I have had an e-mail communication about. And the second point is I'm not -- I wasn't sure whether Mr. Hedaraly was saying that they're going to be bar table documents about this specific incident or bar table documents about many different killings that are not necessarily related to the ones in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct. All the additional -- that is why it is taking quite some time to put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait and see. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 5308 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And, in the meantime, Mr. Dupud, let me ask you, in paragraph 2 of your statement you mentioned various locations where shells fell in the town of Obrovac itself. And the picture that will come up on the screen is one that you marked yesterday and I provided hard copies to the Bench and to the Defence. The only difference between the version in e-court and the hard copies is the number on the top right, but the substance of the markings has not changed. So the version in e-court should be the one what is admitted into evidence but for reference we can use the hard copies. It's a two-page document. If I could also provide a hard copy to the witness. Now, on that -- on that first page that you have that shows the entire lay-out of the town of Obrovac. First of all, let me ask you is that a picture of the town of Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you have marked on this map the locations where you saw shells fall. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, just for the Chamber's information this is a picture from south to north or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. I believe the mountains in the background on the top of the picture are the Velebit, so it would be south to north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: South to north. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Maybe the witness can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from south to north.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Court what the location you've identified as letter A is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter A is the factory, a -- the trio factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what did that factory produce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sports clothes. Sweatshirts, shirts, and trunks, swimming trunks and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you say you were the director of a textile factory. Is that the same textile factory that you have marked as A?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did this factory produce any military clothes or any other military goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to the second picture, which is essentially just a portion of this picture enlarged focused on the more central part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you please tell the Court what you have identified with the letter B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B? The letter B is the very centre of Obrovac, the place where the restaurant, the main town restaurant is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you said there was a shell that hit there. Did it hit on the restaurant itself or in the square in front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Which one is it? On the building, in front, or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The building itself. It is very unlikely in Obrovac for something to fall on Obrovac and not to hit anything, because it is very densely populated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was that restaurant or cafe used by the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a cafe. I don't know exactly how to describe it, but at this time it was closed. During the war, most of these facilities that could serve liquor were closed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So this building was not used by anyone. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were people living above it, because it is an apartment building -- well, actually, above the cafe was an apartment and there were people living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know who was living there? Were they civilians or military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let's move to the right of the picture. What you have as letter C, can you please identify what that building is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: C identifies the health clinic in Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, was that a health clinic used by the military or by civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was there a separate health clinic for the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely for this reason, so that there would be no excuse provided to shell these targets, the medical facility for soldiers was about 15, or more precisely 12, kilometres away from Obrovac at the hydroelectric power plant where there was an infirmary that was used for treating soldiers and -- or just giving them first aid and then, if necessary, evacuating them. So this clinic here was not used for soldiers, for treating soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You say precisely for this reason. How did you know that that is the reason for which a military clinic was located 12 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know because I was the one who issued the order while I was still on active duty for the medical clinic to be moved out of Obrovac. In part also for practical reasons, because if the -- the other side, the enemy side, did not wish to enter Obrovac, they couldn't. It was only possible by opening fire from two intersections and in this case it would be logical to take wounded people into Obrovac and then from Obrovac to Knin. So the purpose was to have the clinic in a location that would serve the need of -- for evacuation. This was a larger facility, but there was another one about 18 kilometres from there. So, in other words, in Muskovci there was a small clinic and the larger one is in Muskovci which was used for treatment of more substantial assistance, it was in the Kastel, the Zegar Kastel. I did not mention this in my statement but I'm just saying it now for clarification purposes. In other words, there was absolutely no need to use the Obrovac medical facility for treatment of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And finally if I can you ask you what you have marked as letter D on this -- on this picture, can you please tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: D is where the police station in Obrovac is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can just have the -- the full picture again. And if I could have the usher's assistance for the witness to identify where his apartment was in the -- in the town. I didn't have that included because there was a chance of protective measures, but now that can be added.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So if you could please point where your apartment was on this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here, on the third floor of this building that I have just marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There are two more locations in your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, the marking, if it is the building on the north side of the river, then it is just a dot. Is that ... then it might be difficult for others to find. Could you add a letter to that. That would then be the letter E negotiation to where you marked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure if this is visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I see it now. We can describe it also more easily. For the record, the witness marked approximately the third apartment building from the left at the north side of the river. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There are two more locations in your statement where you said that shells fell, the bus station and the cultural club or movie theatre. Can those be seen on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No. No, they can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The fortress is blocking the view. It's right underneath that you can find the cultural hall and the cinema is about 150 metres from the police station on the right-hand Zrmanja river bank and it's east of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you're talking about the fortress you're talking about the location to the right of the police station we can see an elevated hill with ruins of a -- that is a castle you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Yes, the fortress is on the left river-bank. And that same river-bank is the bus terminal, about 500 metres to the east of the fortress.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And one last series of questions on this photograph. These buildings that we see on this photograph, were any of these used by the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can I have the 65 ter 5308, the two pages admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The marking is on then on the second page. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, the original is a two-page document. However, markings were then made on one of these pages later so it should be two exhibits, the first one the original one as uploaded into e-court, and then the second one is the second page now marked by the witness in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Is there any reason to have one exhibit the first page unmarked, just with a mark on the second page? It is just going to be one less exhibit but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is also one possibility but since you introduced them as one exhibit. So we then split them up. The first one is the document marked outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter 05308 and it becomes Exhibit number P549.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P549 is admitted into evidence. Then we have the second document on which markings A, B, C, and D appear made out of court and markings added in the court. Mr. Registrar that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P550 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm really sorry. I know it is my fault. The first exhibit is the two pages with the markings made out of court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think you asked now to have the first of the two pages, that is the stretch photograph with markings A, B, C and D made out the court, that is the first exhibit now, from what I understand, Mr. Registrar. Then the second document now is the detailed photograph on which markings appeared already I said A, B, C, D, but that's wrong. It is just B, C, and D there. I made a mistake, and markings added in the courtroom. Yes, I had forgotten that A is outside of the scope of this second exhibit. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we please have D249 on the screen, please, and go to page 2 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, what will come up on the screen is a -- is a map of the town of Obrovac with some markings made on them. I am going to ask you some questions about those markings. Thank you. First of all, looking at this map, can you confirm that the location of the police station and of the bridge, which was M-o-s-t in B/C/S, is accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you also see that there's a hotel that is identified. Was there in fact a hotel at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And was that hotel at the time used by the special police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: During your time in Obrovac, was this hotel ever used by the special police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know where the special police was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several different places, as needed. Or for whatever reason. The last location used was the village of Golubic. Beforehand they would mostly use the Zegar location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how far is the village of Golubic from the town of Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 15 or 16 kilometres. It is difficult to say, because all these are major villages. When I talk about these villages and express these distances, I mean the centres of these villages. For example, Obrovac to Golubic and then when I talk about Zegar and Kastel, when I say distance is 15 kilometres or 18, I mean their respective centres. The far end of Zegar would be about 22 kilometres. When I say 15 I mean centre to centre, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Maybe we can clarify then. When you said that you knew that the location -- last location used was the village of Golubic, did you know where in the village of Golubic and how far that was from the town of Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the school building in Golubic, 15 kilometres to Obrovac, nearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And this hotel in Obrovac, what was it used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly, not -- mostly what hotels are normally used for. Hosting people. This was summertime. Nobody expected the clashes to start escalating. Obrovac has about 22 or 23 kilometres of coast line so one of those catering facilities and there was another minor one that continued to operate throughout the war, yes, that they were operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just noticed my question was not very specific. I wanted to know what it was used for in 1995, in the summer. Would your answer be the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can turn now on the top to the Glinica factory. Are you familiar with that factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what was that factory producing in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: August 1995, it wasn't producing anything at all. The factory closed down in the early 1980s. I think 1981. It had only operated for a very brief while. For the most part it produced nothing at all. The factory soon closed down. Apart from the admin building nothing remained intact, even before the war, 14 or 15 years before the war, it wasn't operating at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In August 1995, were there -- were there -- was it used for any other purposes than the factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't see what purpose it might possibly have been used for. It was a simple ruin about 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And we also see right below that what is the forward command post of the 4th Light Brigade, IZM, 4th Light Brigade. Now you were the commander of the 4th Light Infantry Brigade until 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The forward command post of the brigade command was not there. It wasn't the Glinica factory or in its admin building back in 1995. The front line was just one and a half kilometres from the Glinica factory. A brigade commander putting his command post within snipers' range would not be a very clever commander. My office used to be there up until 1995, my office not my command post, up until 1995, up until Operation Maslenica. The 22nd or the 23rd, the command post was moved first to the village of Bilisane which was the closest, one part of the command post. The other part of command post was moved to the front line in Jasenice. In one of the admin buildings of the local mine there was a part of a battalion that was there. You should chase this information yourself if you want to be more accurate about it, but the forward command post of the brigade 15 days later was moved to Velebit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to clarify something. You said it was there until 1995, the 22nd or 23rd of January. Now should that be 1993 that it was moved after the Maslenica operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1993, yes, if I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure what was moved there at this point so if we could get more clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: One step at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I said 1995, I misspoke. 1993. The command post of the brigade command of the 4th Light Brigade was, conditionally speaking, at this position until the 22nd of January, 1993. The 23rd of January 1993 it was moved and it was never at this location again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In August 1995, where was the command post of the 4th Light Brigade located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The command post of the 4th Light Brigade in August 1995 was at Velebit. There was a facility that was built there, the location itself was Caber. Should be able to see that on a map. East of Lipovaca about 3500 metres or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is a location identified in the next map that I will show you. We'll get to it in just a few minutes. Before you get to that I just want to follow up on the command post. You left the military in 1993. Did you have any interactions with the RSK military between 1993 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obrovac is too small for everyone not to know exactly what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the first part of the witness's answer was not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll ask him. The question that was put to you was whether you had any interactions with the RSK military between 1993 and 1995. And then the second part was that -- of your answer apparently was "Obrovac is too small for everyone not to know exactly what was going on." Now, I heard the first part of your answer, something about concrete. Could you please repeat the first part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have any official or unofficial for that matter contacts with the army of Republika Srpska or with the command of the 4th Light Brigade. After I left the unit, after I was demobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And when you say the army of the Republika Srpska, are you referring to the Republika Srpska or to the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: One last location on the map in front of you at the bottom there is a reference to air defense position, Pzo Polozaji, which I'm probably mispronouncing, were you aware of any such positions in this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I know for certain that up until 1993 the brigade of which I was commander did not have any anti-aircraft weapons or equipment. I often walked to Krusevo and I had to pass this place on my way, but I did not notice any positions, nor did I know anything to indicate that between 1993 and 1995 there were any anti-aircraft that were given to this brigade. Again, Obrovac had 20.000 [as interpreted] inhabitants. It was a very small town. I don't think something of that magnitude could have passed unnoticed in my case or anyone else's.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 5310 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in the, meantime, let me ask you a question I forgot to ask you earlier. When we made the correction to your statement that you had asked to be released from military duties in 1993, can you tell the Court why you made that request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a personal feeling, something that I feel myself. This doesn't make any sense to me now. It didn't even then. It simply wasn't consistent with my own views on how these things should be dealt.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not physically hear the last part of the witness's answer. Could the witness please be asked to repeat clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer, which was not --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And also please maybe clarify what is meant by "this."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps repeat the whole of your answer so that we know exactly -- you said it was a personal feeling, where Mr. Hedaraly would like to know what "it" refers to. That something you said that I feel myself, this doesn't make any sense to you now and that it didn't even then. It simple wasn't consistent with your views on how these things could be dealt. Could you elaborate and repeat also what you further said in your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, I'm deeply convinced that the politicians wanted to resolve this, it would have been feasible. I'm not a politician, I'm an engineer myself, but I'm sure the war could have been avoided. It didn't make sense to me. I didn't think there was a point to all that fighting, and this continues to apply today for me. I don't know what the meaning was of all that fighting. I don't know who is to gain anything. That is just my view. I was involved simply because I had no alternative but at one point I simply took the decision to leave, regardless of the consequences, I no longer wanted any part in that because I was very suspicious about what the possible outcome might be. And that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In the summer of 1995, in the weeks preceding Operation Storm, were you ever asked to -- to rejoin the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some contacts off the record, but I refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We have a map on the screen, which is a map that you marked outside of court. But before we show the markings, this is an quite a few of them, I want to orient the Court. Can I have the cursor on the town of Obrovac. So where the cursor is, that's the town of Obrovac, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you go down south at the bottom of the map, a little bit to the left, that's the town of Benkovac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we go back up to Obrovac and follow the road going east and then north, that yellow road, what does that lead to? What town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Racac and on to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you just tell the Court generally speak where Knin is located with respect to this map. It's off the map, but in what direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we could please have the usher assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obrovac, and then you follow this route. The road here in the middle and then Knin lies to the east. There should be a marking there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you take the road to Benkovac, there is an junction and then there is a road that forks off to the right and that is the road that will eventually take to you Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't need these saved, Your Honour. If we can move to 65 ter 5309, which is the version of this map that witness has signed -- has marked and those are hard copies provided as well and I have one for the witness as well. Madam Usher, please. And once again, Your Honour, the only difference between the hard copies and the version is e-court is the number in the top right in red. Maybe I can start before it comes up on the screen since everyone has hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we all have hard copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court first of all what the dotted line represents that is on the top of the map going down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The dotted line up there represents the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The front line between ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 4th of August, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And is that where the Croatian -- sorry. Is that where the RSK troops were located, along that front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just to the right of the front line this is an little triangle with a vertical line on top of it. Can you please identify what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the forward command post of the command of the 4th Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Finally, in your statement at paragraph 4, you state that the shelling extended to smaller villages around Obrovac. My first question is before going to those locations what is the basis of your knowledge regarding these areas being shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question is logical because Obrovac is in a canyon. It's very difficult to actually see Obrovac from outside this canyon. Nevertheless two or three times I went to Zegar to see my family, because it was obvious that this operation had a radical objective, on the one hand and on the other, the first time I went was about 11.00 and the next time was about 4.00 p.m., and yet I did climb up to the fortress several times just for myself, just so I would know what to do about leaving Obrovac and perhaps moving my family somewhere safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We only have a short time remaining before the break, so the areas that you mentioned in your statement that were being shelled, those are the ones that you circled on this map? If we could have the full view again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if I could just run through the remembers for you. If you can confirm for me. K was for Krusevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's the Obrovac-Knin-Benkovac junction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then the letters ZE are for Zelengrad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Zelengrad, or rather, yes, Zelengrad. But this road separating Krusevo from Zelengrad this is the boundary between the two villages, so this village could be about Krusevo, it could be about Zelengrad, but when you take this road you pass these and you see it. But one thing I want to say is I don't know if the villages were shelled that you can't see from the road. I don't know that. The only places I marked were the places that I could actually see. There is nothing here that I didn't see myself. I witnessed all of this myself so that's that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could just get foundation of why he was on that road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could have done in cross as well but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: He just said he saw it personally. I don't have time. The break is almost there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can deal with the matter on cross. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The letters Bi is for Bilisane. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the letters Bo for Bogatnik? 10

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the Z with the diacritic zhu [phoen], that is for Zegar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zegar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we go up Za is for Zaton, up and to the left? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And M is for Muskovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I think you just stated, just to confirm, these are all areas that you yourself saw personally shells falling, right, these circles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: My final question for you is to your knowledge, were there any military facilities in any of the areas that were shelled that you have circled on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing, perhaps. There is one exception, Kastel Zegarski where there was a factory, the Trikotasa [phoen] factory, about 200.000 square metre, there was a kitchen that was used to prepare food for members of the 4th Light Brigade, so that was the only exception. That was that. All the rest was nothing in that sense. But the other question is there was no other route I could have taken to see my family. I had two sisters. One was in Bilisane, which is -- 150 metres. I know probably you will be asking why she went to Muskovci. And then I had sister who is probably [indiscernible]. It is an answer to your question, that's what I mean, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No problem. Can I please have this exhibit marked and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit P551.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P551 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dupud.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That concludes my direct examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We are close to a break. I would have one additional question for you, Mr. Dupud. You told us how civilians were leaving. You said some took their own transportation, other took buses. It was earlier in the morning. Were these regular buses, were these buses specifically ordered for this transportation? Could you tell us about these buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regular buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us, was there -- how many buses were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a company, I think they had about 20 buses. They were professional haulers. I don't know how many they were using at that time, but, yes, these buses were being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, now, in Obrovac, how many buses did you see? I think that you said you observed yourself, your family, your wife, and I think said one of your children leaving. How many buses did you see at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember specifically, and I don't wish to speculate. I can't say right now how many buses there were. They would normally appear at about 7.00 in the morning. The first buses left Obrovac at 10.00 in the morning. One went to Zelengrad, one to Bilisane. In principle there should have been a minimum of three. That's what the regular lines were. There was no one in Krusevo. Therefore, there was nothing there, so as a matter of principle, a minimum of three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They were heading for where, these buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These villages around Obrovac, regular lines to Bilisani, Zelengrad, Zegar, Muskovci, there was a bus going to each of these villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that was not the destination your wife was choosing, was she?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. My wife didn't take that bus. I stayed in Obrovac and she drove with a relative to Zegar, or, rather, drove with a friend to her relative's place in Zegar. She did not take a bus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the buses were the normal line buses as you would see them everyday. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Then one final question. The population, is that 2.000 or 20.000, of Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two, two, about 2.000, 2.500. During the war, even less, because most people moved to some of the surrounding villages 2.000, 2.500. The municipality itself had about 12.000, maybe 12.500.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. It appeared as 20.000 on the transcript. We will have a break and we'll then resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. You may proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Dupud. Let me clarify again something that was briefly discussed during your direct examination. Between January 1993 and August of 1995, you had no military role. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between January 1993 -- could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: From the time of your demobilisation after the Maslenica operation until the beginning of Operation Storm, you had no military function. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, you didn't have a military function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't. From September 1993 up until the end of the war, I had no role.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: From September 1993 until the end of the war, did you have any political function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, finally, from September 1993 to the end of the war, did you have any other governmental function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was the general manager of a factory, and for a while, I was a representative in the municipal assembly of the Obrovac municipality, if you can call that a government role. I think this was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the dates that you were a member of the municipal assembly of Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can't, because I don't know exactly, because this was not a political function of any kind. I was just a representative of a group of citizens, and I was not a member of any political party, so it wasn't really all that important. I think this was at the end of 1994 or the beginning of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you were a member of the municipal assembly in June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In May 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was. Up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your witness statement at paragraph 4, you mention a man by the name of Dragomir Vukcevic who was the last to leave Obrovac at about 5.00 a.m. on the morning of the 5th. Can you explain to the Court who Dragomir Vukcevic was or is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragomir Vukcevic was the president of the municipal assembly of Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was he something to the effect of the mayor of Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, he was the mayor of Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall the name Radivoje Paravinja, and if you do, can you please explain to the Court who Radivoje Paravinja was in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radivoje Paravinja was the major of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and he was the commander of the 4th Light Brigade. That was his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that with respect to events in August 1995 concerning the activities of the civilian government of Obrovac that the mayor, Mr. Vukcevic was in a better position to know what the civilian authorities in Obrovac were doing, than you were in August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the activities of the 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac, in August of 1995, would you agree with me that Radivoje Paravinja is in a better position to know what the 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac, was doing in August 1995 than you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to turn, first, to 1D37-0001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, this is the statement that was given to the Office of the Prosecutor by the mayor of Obrovac on 21 February 2007. The first thing I'd like to ask you about this statement is that the date of the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor is identical to the date of the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. So my first question to you is: Were you together with Mr. Vukcevic meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 21st of February, 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not with Vukcevic at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You say at that time. Were you with Vukcevic at some other time in 2007?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suppose yes. I saw him quite frequently because he is in Belgrade, and I am in Belgrade, so from time to time we meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you have conversations with Mr. Vukcevic about the fact that both of you were going to be giving statements to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you and Mr. Vukcevic discuss the events on the 4th of August, 1995 -- the events of the 4th of August, 1995, at any time in 2006, 2007, or 2008?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not only with him, I did not discuss them with anyone. I just want to erase them from my memory, all those events. And other than my family, I don't discuss these events with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is some ambiguity in the answer. The question was whether the witness discussed the events on the 4th of August, and then the answer was, "Not only with him, I did not discuss them with anyone." So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the exception of the investigators of The Hague Tribunal. But that is implied, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the answer is that you did not discuss it. Not only not with him, that would be the answer the witness apparently wants to give. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one brief point. Before we turn to the statement of someone else I think -- just want to make sure that we have established a procedure that -- to make sure that the question is first asked of the witness or is in the statement or testimony already before confronting him with an alleged inconsistency. I just want to make sure that -- I thought that's what we had agreed on. I don't know whether the question is obvious but just to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure what Mr. Hedaraly is referring to, but I believe the entire statement of the mayor is inconsistent with the version that we heard this morning and that is precisely why I wish to confront him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, Mr. Hedaraly is suggesting a certain procedure in confronting the witness after a question has been put to him on matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: At the very at least what we can do is we can start with a portion of his testimony or his statement that Mr. Misetic changing and then if he wants to go to someone else's statement, that's fine --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: -- but otherwise, I think that's what I think we've -- I mean, I believe I was once here and that's what the Chamber had told to us do or maybe I'm mistaken, but that was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe he is -- I believe he is mistaken, Your Honour. Last time Mr. Hedaraly and I were in court we went through this exact procedure with them confronting the witness with a statement from his mother, and that's precisely the same thing I intend to do, nothing -- nothing anything different. If there's specifically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see, Mr. Hedaraly, if you have any problems, then we will hear from you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First, Mr. Dupud, you are aware, are you not, that the authorities of Obrovac, on many occasions prior to Operation Storm would evacuate the civilian population. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And these were organised evacuations. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depends on your viewpoint, how you understand evacuation, but I state here, please allow me to finish, that the -- 50 per cent of the evacuations from Obrovac were done on a private basis. People just left --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 90 per cent, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- so the Obrovac inhabitants who had houses in the villages or relatives there, they left on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When I say organised evacuation, I mean, first, the authorities would tell people to leave. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the statement. Paragraph 2, Mr. Vukcevic told the Office of the Prosecutor: "I was elected mayor of Obrovac in January 1994." At paragraph 4, he says: "There was a conflict between the Croatian army and the army of the Krajina during this time and the warning sirens would sound and we would have to evacuate the women, children, and the elderly temporarily to the hills to be out of range of the shelling. We would evacuate them to Bogatnik, Zegar, or Krupa. This type of evacuation happened several times up until August 1995." My question to you, sir, is: You are aware that the authorities would evacuate civilians to the villages of Bogatnik, Zegar and Krupa on various occasions, isn't that correct, before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I reiterate, the evacuation of inhabitants was done. People left Obrovac on several occasions in the course of 1993, 1994, and 1995. However, I have to stress one point here. This statement is not correct, simply for the reason that after 1993, I think it was in May, a shell which was randomly fired from someplace, fell into the Zrmanja River some 15 metres from the high school playground which was at that time full of children. There were about 200 children there. After this, not a single parent would allow their children to go to school, because there would have been a tragedy had this shell hit the playground. And the statement here that the evacuation was planned and done on orders from the municipal authorities, I simply claim it is not true and probably the mayor wanted to -- felt that he was more important than he was and he wanted to project that image here. That's all I'm claiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question that I asked you. You are aware that the civilian authorities prior to Operation Storm had conducted evacuations to the villages of Bogatnik, Zegar, and Krupa. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that people left Obrovac, seeking shelter in 1993, 1994, and 1995, and I'm almost certain that there was not an organised evacuation and that the authorities did not play a big role in this. I don't know why anyone should be evacuated if they had a home in Bogatic [as interpreted]. They would just leave Obrovac on their own and go to Bogatic or Zegar -- Bogatnik or Zegar with the exception of a few people who went to the Krupa monastery. These were old-time inhabitants of Obrovac and I can assume that maybe this was organised by the municipal authorities. I am referring here to the people from Obrovac and Croats, and other people from Obrovac who were from Obrovac originally. So it is possible that this was organised to accommodate these people on the premises of the Krupa monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to paragraph 5 of the statement, talking about the evacuation on the morning of the 4th of August. The mayor says: "At about 5.00 a.m. on the 4th of August, 1995, I heard the sound of shelling in the town. I heard the warning siren which warned us that the town was going to be shelled again. Shells fell within 200 metres of my house. The women, children, and the elderly were evacuated to Krupa. People who cars," it should say, "people with cars travelled to Krupa themselves and those who had no transport gathered at the bus station and were bussed to Krupa." Isn't that what happened on the morning of the 4th of August, 1995, Mr. Dupud?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't see a major difference between what Mr. Vukcevic said and what I have said. He does not claim here that anything was organised. I said, if you remember, and I think you do, that some people, in other words those who did not have their own vehicles, travelled on the buses, the regular line buses. Because, at that time, there was no other possibility to use any other meanings of transportation, so it wasn't even necessary to organise anything if there were buses there any way. And I think that the mayor here also mentioned Krupa. So it is only those people who had nowhere to go. They were the one who is were accommodated in Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you what I think the difference is and see if you agree with me. Paragraph 5, there's a portion of the sentence further on down that he says: "Although we had been through this evacuation process before ..." And then if you go down to paragraph 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And we can put that on the screen for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He says: "At about 11.30 a.m., on the 4th of August, 1995, the mayor of Benkovac, Stevo Vuksa, telephoned me and asked why we had evacuated the people from the town. He was angry, saying that by evacuating the civilians it would weaken the front line. But that I understood he meant that if the civilians left, then the soldiers would follow their families. I explained that we always did this when the siren sounded and when we were being shelled and that we would be bringing the people back later when the situation calmed down." So do you agree with me that the mayor of the town seems to have told the Office of the Prosecutor that this was an organised evacuation of the civilians out of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot give you any answer to this. I can't say either that he stated that it was organised or not organised. I don't know how to interpret his statement. I wasn't there when he spoke with Vuksa which was a long time ago, but I do have something that I would like to clarify regarding the organised evacuation of citizens. On the 24th of January, 1993, I was the brigade commander. I received information at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we're going to go back to 1993, I'd that if they want to do it in redirect, but I'm trying to keep --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're putting the questions, if you think that the witness is no longer in the area where your question relates to, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can cut him off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, within--

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm used to usually asking the Judge to do that but if you wish me to do it, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's say, if I allow the parties to do it if they use this --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Judiciously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If they do it -- and if they do it in such a way that -- well, let's say to similar to what I would have done, of course I do not expect any witness do dwell on matters which are not part of the question. Yes, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I completely agree with that but, I mean, the question asks typically about the organised evacuation of the civilians out of the town and he refers to the statement of the mayor of Obrovac who says it happened this way before. Now the witness wants to clarify what has happened before. It is within the ambit of his question. If he doesn't want to hear the answer, he shouldn't ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Hedaraly is more than welcome to ask in redirect if he thinks there is some connection to this question. My question was clearly related to the 4th of August and whether there was evacuation on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your question was related to the statement and the statement contains, "I explained that we always did this when the siren sounded," which means that if you take him to that statement, then of course you can't say that it is just limited to the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I understand and this is why it is difficult for me to cut a witness off. So, if we could get guidance from the Trial Chamber when they start to go off, to bring them back to focus on the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So here I agree with Mr. Hedaraly, that it is not exclusively the 4th of August, but of course if you wanted to take him back. But let's now, Witness, you started saying something about what happened in an earlier year, that's the 24th of January, 1993. Did you want to refer to any evacuation event that happened in 1994? Is that what you were -- then briefly explain. We'll focus on the 4th, but if there is any relevance to what happened earlier, then please tell us briefly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to clarify and show what the connection between an organised departure and not organised. So I'm talking about the 24th of January, 1993. This was when the first evacuation took place. It was so organised, let me just point this out, that I tried to prevent it. So had it been organised I'm sure I would have had a say in it. But the population, the people just left, 90 per cent of them had their cars. You couldn't prevent them from leaving. So this was similar. I just wanted to point out this fact that all these departures, all these occasions when people left Obrovac and went to the villages around Obrovac, were really something that people themselves did of their own will, and in no way could we call them organised. And I mentioned the 24th, because that's the one that I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could have paragraph 9 on the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "At about 6.00 p.m. the same day a friend of mine, Nebojsa Mijic came to me and told me that he had received information that the civilians were being evacuated from Benkovac. I was angry after my earlier conversation with the mayor of Benkovac, and so I rang him and asked what was going on. He said that they were evacuating the civilians toward Srb. I asked why he was do that, and he refused to say but told me to tell our civilian protection to contact Babic in Knin who was head of the civil protection in Knin." And at paragraph 10: "I told our civilian protection to ring the civil protection in Knin. But there was no reply. They then tried the local civil police but again could get no information. At about 10.00 p.m. on the 4th August I had contact with the local ARSK brigade commander, Rajko Paravinja and he came to see me at the civil protection office and told me that a wider conflict was expected and that the civilians should be evacuated to Srb which was to be the planned collection place for the civilians. As a result, we began to organise the evacuation. Our civil protection staff split up and went to all the surrounding villages to organise the evacuation." Then at paragraph 11: "At about 11.00 p.m. I got to Krupa with another member of the civil protection and told the civilians there to organise themselves and get ready to be evacuated. I returned to Obrovac at about 4.00 a.m. on the 5th of August to collect some documentation from my house. The town was deserted but relatively undamaged." Now, Mr. Dupud, the civilians left the Obrovac municipality towards Srb under an organised evacuation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I remember this vividly and I will try to explain it. I don't know how Nebojsa Mijic could have said at 6.00 to the mayor and how he could be angry because of his conversation with the mayor of the Benkovac municipality, which was -- which took place later on. I don't understand this. You said that Savo Vuksa called the president of the municipal assembly or the mayor of Obrovac at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 6.00 p.m., which is 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At 11.00. We can check this. And he called him at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You may a translation issue there, sir. It says -- that the mayor he called the mayor of Benkovac at 6.00 p.m. which military time is 1800?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just have to clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have in paragraph 8 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the time of 11.30, and then in paragraph 9, we have -- no -- yes, paragraph 9 we have 6.00 p.m. So when we're talking about times of telephone conversations, let's clearly distinguish between what happened at -- according to this statement, at least that at 11.30 on the 4th of August, the mayor of Benkovac called the mayor of Obrovac, and then at 9.00 -- then at 6.00 p.m. that same day, that is therefore early evening, the -- a friend called the mayor of Obrovac and explained. That's what the statement says so let's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But I don't think he understands that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, depends. Let's put the questions to him and always specify clearly which telephone conversation you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify this with you, sir. What the mayor here, and see if you agree with me, the mayor is saying, the mayor of Obrovac is saying that the mayor of Benkovac called him at 11.30 in the morning to complain about the fact that the mayor of Obrovac earlier that morning had evacuated the civilian population. And then he says the mayor of Obrovac later learned at 6.00 p.m. that the mayor of Benkovac was now doing the same thing that the mayor of Obrovac will done in the morning and for which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, do you understand now? Do you understand now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You are -- are you aware that the civil protection of the Obrovac municipality went out into the villages on the evening of the 4th to tell civilians who were in the villages that they had to prepare to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the evening, yes. That's what I said in my statement, isn't it? The first group of civilians leaving. So that was the amendments that we entered, 8.00 p.m., 2000 hours the first group left and this wasn't an organised thing. The first group left in no organised evacuation, those who left who had somewhere to go, who had families or homes perhaps in Serbia, that was the first group, but by 8.00 there had been no organised evacuation nor had any calls been made by the civilian authorities to leave Obrovac or the other villages for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Putting aside the issue of what happened on the morning of the 4th, you now agree with me that the decision to move civilians from the Obrovac municipality to Srb was a decision to make an organised evacuation, in the evening of the 4th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't agree, nor can I disagree. I'm simply not aware of that decision. I can't say whether it is true or false.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where is the decision in the -- I see all kind of activities described, but I do not see any decision here. Could you assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean he told -- Radivoje Paravinja came to see me at the civil protection office and told me that a wider conflict was expected and that the civilians should be evacuated to Srb, which was to be the planned collection centre for the civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you call that a decision. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What time did you leave Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Earlier on I had left Obrovac twice that day at a quarter to midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In your statement at paragraph 4, you say: "The members of the civil protection and the president of the municipality, I think is Dragomir Vukcevic, were the last to leave at around 5.00 a.m." If you left at a quarter to midnight, how do you know that the civil protection and Mr. Vukcevic left at 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They left after me and we met up in Belgrade. It was then that they told me that they had left Obrovac, or, rather, Krupa at 5.00 a.m. So this is not direct knowledge. This is indirect knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And in those conversations after the fact, did they also tell you that the reason -- the reason that the civil protection and the mayor of the town were the last to leave was because the civil protection was responsible for organising the evacuation of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't go that far when I talked to them. I simply had no stamina at the time to have any long conversations about that. We met briefly, when did you leave, right, when did you leave and how about yourself, and that was about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dupud.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could call up 1D37-0012. Your Honour, I will tender the at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that, Your Honour. I think witness statements are not typically admissible unless the rules of 92 bis, ter or quater have been fulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. We will call a witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Relevant portions have been -- yes, whether there is any need to that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll decide that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but suggest that it will be Defense case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could meanwhile give further guidance to the parties. I think you find what I had in mind as whether or not to confront the witness with the statement of another witness, that, I think at the time I gave the guidance that it should not be done if the matter was not dealt with yet in his own statement or in examination-in-chief so you can't just confront the witness with someone's else statement on a certain matter. If no questions have been asked to that witness about the same event. If, however, that is done, then there's no need to repeat that and you find that at page 4861 to 4863.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that was my only concern, because we didn't know what was coming up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I don't think until now that is a major problem. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just one possibly minor point of clarification, Your Honour. I noted it came up in the course of a redirect examination, and that is I would assume, but I'm seeking guidance from the Court, that in -- in cases where the matter has been raised in a witness's statement and therefore there's no need to put a question of the type that is referred to in the Court's guidance, that there would still be reference to that portion of the statement that is at issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because otherwise, the witness would not know exactly what his statement would have been on that. But I don't think that we have any real problems at this moment. So let's then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dupud, what we have on the screen here is the report of the commander of the 4th Light Brigade of Obrovac that he sent to his superior officers on the 9th of August, 1995 reporting on what happened on the 4th of August, 1995. It is a document by Mr. Paravinja, Radivoje Paravinja. The first sentence says: "The enemy commenced the artillery attack on 4 August 1995 at 0500 hours. At 6.20 hours four aircrafts fired rockets at Celavac and in the area of the village of Golubic." If you go down to the middle of that first paragraph. Captain reports: "In the evening at around 2300 hours the evacuation of the civilian population started. Our units were well supported by the artillery of the 4th Brigade and the 7th Corps Artillery Group. On 5 August 1995 we were still firmly holding our positions." Now let me ask you, Mr. Dupud, you seem to have known a lot of information about the 4th Light Brigade even on the 4th of August you were able to draw on a map the forward command post of the 4th Light Brigade in the mountains of the Velebit which I assume ordinary civilians probably would not have known, in Obrovac. What type of artillery support did the 4th Light Brigade of Obrovac have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I can comment on this combat report. I do believe, however, that some of the information here is inaccurate, as far as support is concerned, I can tell you that this is the 7th Artillery Corps group. Were they providing support or not is not something that I can tell you. As for the command post, the forward command post or relocated command post, we have some information because I set it up in 1993 and it never moved until 1995, and that's the only reason I know, not because I had anything else to do with it or because we had any other type of contact with the commander of the 4th Light Brigade. That command post was there since the 24th or the 25th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's continue on here because it relates to the map and the villages that you say were shelled. He further reports: "The Ustasha accomplished a breach through Crveni Potoci [phoen] towards Mole Zuljine in the AOR of the 15th corps.
