As our flank was endangered we assigned a company to our right flank and two tanks T-34 and two armoured personnel carriers and in this manner we secured the brigade's right flank." My question to you is, as you were travelling around in the Obrovac municipality did you see the artillery support groups, did you see ARSK T-34s, did you see ARSK armoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first I hear of it, about this unit having tanks. First I hear of it, which implies that I certainly didn't see it. I don't know. I don't know where something like that would have come from. Actually, I can't comment. What I mean is I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It goes on: "At 1000 hours," and this is now on the 5th, "the Ustasha emerged at Stikada near Gracac so we could not use this route for evacuation. Having assured ourselves that the civilians had been evacuated from Benkovac and that the major part of the army was already in Ervenik, I ordered the brigade to evacuate according to the plan towards Zegar and further towards Mokro Polje." I will stop right there. You say that you yourself went to Zegar. Did you see the soldiers of the 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac, in Zegar with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I knew this statement is accurate. All I can add is this. I left Zegar and took the Zegar-Golubic-Gracac road out. On the morning of the 5th there were no Croatian soldiers in Gracac or in Stikada. I was there, but I can't comment on Mr. Paravinja's statement simply because I have no information about this. It may be true, it may not be true. I really cannot comment apart from what I said and what I said was I left the territory and took the road through Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to clarify something and perhaps I'm mistaken. I think the question referred to RSK troops and he talked about Croatian soldiers in the town just to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I agree, and I was going to clarify that with him as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hedaraly, perhaps you give an opportunity first and then if the confusion persists, then to intervene. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You may have heard Mr. Hedaraly's comment. What I was asking you was, did you see ARSK soldiers in Zegar on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wasn't in Obrovac before August, not in Obrovac, I couldn't see why I said after midnight I left -- or rather before midnight I left Obrovac and then right after midnight I left Zegar as well. You see what I'm saying. Therefore on the 5th of August and there's no way I can see anything, and that's why I can't comment on all of this, everything you are telling me, it is simply not true. I didn't see any soldiers of the Republika Srpska Krajina in Zegar and Golubic, because for me, this is something entirely new. I don't know this. I wasn't there. I simply wasn't physically present and I can't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think the interpreter is having a little problem with your speed. So if you could slow down -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, the speed, right, right, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Where did you wind up on the 5th of August? You said you left Zegar shortly after midnight. Where were you going to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I took the following route, Zegar, Krupa, Golubic, Gracac, Srb, Martin Brod or rather, Bosansko Petrovac and then I spent the night in Banja Luka. That was my exact route.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we continue on with Mr. Paravinja's report, he says: "The unit command evacuated or destroyed the documentation and one part of the ordnance. The whole civilian population was evacuated except for a small number who refused to leave, the units withdrew in an organised manner, following the civilian column." Did you notice, as you were following this route, did you notice behind you military personnel evacuating along the same route you were taking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpretation to the last question was "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can scroll up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Captain Paravinja reports in section 2.1: Evacuated ordnance, this is what he reports on what they had. 105-millimetre Howitzers, two pieces, 76-metre gun D1, two pieces. 76-millimetre gun ZIS, three pieces. 120-millimetre mortar, six pieces, 128-metre light rocket launcher, six pieces. 82-millimetre mortar, nine pieces. And then lists ordnance that remained on the way, which I believe means ordnance that was left behind, T-34 tank, armoured personnel carrier M-63, 40-metre anti-aircraft gun, two pieces. If I can stop right there, and then there's an anti-aircraft gun 20/3? Now, sir, you were asked questions about an anti-aircraft position this morning and I believe you said you didn't believe that the ARSK had any anti-aircraft weapons. Mr. Paravinja reports on the 9th of August that they had at least three pieces, actually more than that, because if you look at the destroyed ordnance section there is three pieces, anti-aircraft gun 20/1 that were destroyed. So at least and then other ordnance, a 40-millimetre, two pieces, anti-aircraft gun 20/1, two pieces. Can you tell the Court, and we can show you a map, if necessary, where did the 4th Light Brigade Obrovac deploy all of its anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never set eyes on this before, 20/3, perhaps, but a tank, no. This is the first time that I see this information suggesting that the 4th Light Brigade had a tank or an APC. I don't have a comment. What I can say is the 4th Light Brigade had no anti-aircraft weapons and the anti-aircraft weapons were not positioned as marked on that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I think you did not accurately reflect what the witness's testimony earlier was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Going by my recollection, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can tell what you he said. He said that "for certain up until 1993 the brigade of which I was a commander did not have anti-aircraft weapons or equipment." That was the first. Then he added to that, that it was Obrovac was a small town that is near the 20.000, which is a mistake. Should be 2.000. I don't think that something of that magnitude could have passed unnoticed -- no. And then he said he walked up -- yes. "I often walked to Krusevo and had to pass this place on my way, but I did not notice any positions nor did I know anything to indicate that." That's what he said and not that, as you put it to him, that the ARSK had no anti-aircraft weapons. That is not what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will correct that, Your Honour. He said he had no knowledge and that he walked around --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: His attention was drawn to a specific place where, allegedly there would have been anti-aircraft. He said "I walked up to that place, I haven't seen it," and he said "until 1993 when I was in command our unit didn't have it."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, I read that differently, Your Honour. It says, "nor did I know anything to indicate that between 1993 and 1995 there were any anti-aircraft given to this brigade," not that there were any anti-aircraft at that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all it is limited to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what I asked him about is the 4th Light Brigade Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- I thought that the question was more broad. But matters have been clarified now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, looking at this list of ordnance it is safe to say that if in fact, Mr. Paravinja's report is accurate, you had no knowledge of where this ordnance was deployed on the 4th of August, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we look at section 2.5, depots, you were asked by Mr. Hedaraly about these villages. You were asked whether there were any military -- I don't want to be wrong and I will have Mr. Hedaraly correct me, please, if I say something wrong but I believe he asked you if there were any military installations or military targets, I'm not sure what the exact phrase was, in those outlying villages. You mentioned Zegar and a kitchen in Zegar. Now if you look at section 2.5, Captain Paravinja reports that the ammunition depot Krupa was destroyed, the quartermaster depot Zegar was destroyed. Were you aware of a quartermaster depot being located in Zegar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. As far as I can remember, I did say that in my evidence. In Zegar, the old school building which was no longer used as a school, the weapons and equipment were stored after the signing of the Vance-Owen Plan. That was that. I have no reason to try and conceal that. And the kitchen was there too and that's as much as I know. Ammunition storage in Krupa, I don't know about that. Ammunition storage in Velebit, I don't know. The medical station in Zegar, that has been explained too, therefore, I don't think there is anything to challenge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, for the precise text of what was included in your question, it is page 60, lines 18 and 19 general reference is made to the ARSK. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would now ask that this exhibit be marked and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D520, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D520 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: One question if we could go back to the first page of this document. Towards the bottom where Mr. Paravinja says: "The withdrawal went well, although Ustasha fired on the units all the way to the village of Zegar." Were you aware that the Croatian army was firing on the units of the 4th Light Brigade of Obrovac and was engaged in a pursuit of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is clear based on my evidence so far, that there's no way I could have known. I said I wasn't involved in the fighting, nor did I know anything to indicate this, were they firing, when, how, along the line of confrontation. I don't think they were exchanging candy. They were probably involved in fighting. As for the rest of it, I really don't know. All of this happened after my departure. I left, I told you when I left, and I don't think any of these questions have any sort of purpose. I don't know what their purpose might be if I said that I left Obrovac on the morning of the 5th right after midnight night and you're asking me about something that occurred at 11.00 or 10.00 in the morning. I don't see any purpose to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, the purpose is, sir, that in much of your statement and in much of your testimony this morning you have indicated that you had subsequent conversation with some of these people so you may have learned some of this information later. So that is why I ask you the question. If we could move on. At paragraph 2 of your statement you say: "On 3 August 1995 the United Nations observers in Obrovac left the area. We therefore suspected something would happen." When you say "we," who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm talking about me and my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we could call up 1D37-0018, please. This is dated 28 July 1995. It is a message from Captain Paravinja to Jordanian Battalion and Canadian battalion of UNPROFOR. It says: "This is to warn you that you should situation worsen you are obligated to execute the responsibilities you have assumed in accordance with the Vance plan and you are not allowed to withdraw. Should you not execute the said responsibilities, we shall be forced to physically block you and any attempt to abandon the zone shall be prevented by force." You made mention of in you statement about the fact that the UN did in fact did leave on the 3rd. Were you aware that the authorities in Obrovac, the military authority had issued a warning to the UN not to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is one thing that needs clarifying. When I said "observers," it was civilian police in Obrovac. I said they left on the 3rd. As for this warning, I have never heard of this before. I have never set eyes on it before. I -- I don't know, I can't comment. I would never have written anything like this myself. No, this is a different kettle of fish altogether. If the commander wrote this, perhaps we should ask somebody else. But then what I said was civilian, meaning civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I ask that this be marked and tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D521.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. D521 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Misetic, this comes down to more or less tendering from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And apparently Mr. Hedaraly has no problem, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I just didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just noticed that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Turning to paragraph 4 of your statement, Witness, you say: "The radio communications system was disturbed and we had no contact with the military or political authorities in Knin." First, can you tell us what radio communications system you are referring to in that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that in one of the statements earlier - I don't know whose it was - mention was made that the repeater on Velebit was shelled around 6.30. From that moment on, there -- it was no longer possible to establish any kind of communication, either phone or radio communications. I could not even listen to the radio from the moment when the repeater was destroyed. That's what I meant. When I say "we," I mean the entire population. I did not mean the unit, the 4th Light Brigade, or the civilian authorities. I meant just civilians, civilian population, which was just another element that contributed to the panic, if I may call it so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So in paragraph 4 what you're referring to there is simply an ordinary radio, that you couldn't listen to the radio from Knin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could also not make any phone calls, so there were no phone lines nor radio communications. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Turning back to the issue of evacuation and you told us at the beginning of this cross-examination that you were a member of the Obrovac municipal council?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Assembly, thank you. If we could turn to 1D37-0028, please, Mr. Registrar. If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is from a book by Milisav Sekulic. Have you had an opportunity to read that book before? The book is called: "Knin fell in Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sekulic would have been your colleague, though, in the military of the ARSK. You know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, General Sekulic came after I left the brigade and I had no chance to meet him. At that time he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me show you what he wrote in his book about the events concerning the fall of the Republika Srpska Krajina. And I will skip around so we don't take too much time to go to the relevant portions but he writes: "The Obrovac municipality is a typical example. The official authorities initiated an action for the collective emigration of the people. The responsible body in this action was the municipal assembly." And if we go down: "It was more than obvious that the events in Western Slavonia had a depressing effect on the population and authorities in Obrovac. Fear became dominant. However, it was indisputable that the streets of Obrovac were always full of officers and conscripts. More of them were in the streets than on their positions. If this behaviour was intended to seek guarantee that the citizens would be preserved from the Ustasha aggression, then who would stop the Croats when they launched the attack?" Finally, if we can turn the page, please. Page 3 of the B/C/S, please. The final portion above the three dots -- sorry, above the page 188 reference. It says: "From the contents of the overview of the situation it is easy to see why the morale of the people and the army was so low and where the announcements of what was to happen on the 4th and 5th of August, 1995, originated from. This form of conduct by the authorities of the Obrovac municipality at the beginning of June 1995 represented the preparation and general evacuation exercise of the people and the army, which was to unfold less than two months later. Preconditions were created, allowing for the people to leave their homes easily at the blink of an eye. It is obvious that this form of preparations and general exercises were more efficient and lethal than all the Croatian lethal assets." Now, sir, General Sekulic writes in his book that the municipality authorities of Obrovac as early as June 1995 were preparing for the general evacuation of the civilians. You told us earlier that you were a member of the assembly in Obrovac. Were you a participant in some of the actions -- or some of the meetings that General Sekulic describes in his book between the municipal authorities of Obrovac and the authorities in Knin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I reserve the right not to say what I think about General Sekulic, but this speaks for itself. Simply, it is not true that the municipal assembly ever discussed or took any decision on an organised evacuation or on organizing the evacuation of Obrovac. He probably has reasons of his own for that, and I wouldn't want to comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me show you 1D37-0020. Do you know who Milan Milic is, while we wait for it come up? Who he was in Obrovac in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know which Milan Milic you mean. There were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, we will see from this document now. I mean the head of municipal civil protection in Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I know whom you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 6 June 1995. It is sent to Knin. The subject is: "Assistance request for the location of clamp yokes for a 06 cable." It says: "Considering we have commenced building rafts on the Zrmanja River in order to evacuate the population in the event of Ustasha aggression," and then it goes on seeking certain equipment so that they can build rafts to cross Zrmanja River if it becomes necessary. Were you aware of these types of preparations in Obrovac in June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obviously someone was playing war games here. This is the first time that I see here and this is the first -- see this and this is the first time that I hear of it. And I don't see where one could use a raft. I simply don't see why a raft would be built in Obrovac. I can't really comment on this. This is the first time I hear of this. This man was not from Obrovac municipality and I know for sure that I did not see him in Obrovac on the 4th. After the 4th of July, I don't know where he was, what his whereabouts were, and as for the raft here, I don't see any purpose. I don't see why one would want a raft. That's in short.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now tender both 1D37-0028, which is the excerpt from the Sekulic book; and I tender 1D37-0020, which is the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D37-0028 becomes Exhibit number D522.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D522 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And 1D37-0020 becomes Exhibit number D523.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D523 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would now like to show you a video, sir, from the 6th of August, which is a footage -- which is 1D37-0025. It is video footage of Obrovac after the Croatian forces had taken the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask -- Sir, you've had a chance to look at that clip. The mayor in his statement to the Office of the Prosecutor at paragraph 11 told the Office of the Prosecutor that when he came back at 4.00 a.m. on the 5th of August to collect some documentation from his house, "the town was deserted but relatively undamaged." Based on everything you saw on the 4th of August, is it also your conclusion that the town was relatively undamaged and -- and -- based on what you've seen in this video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I mean he is referring to the statement of Mr. Vukcevic that can be put to the witness so he can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it's a limited portion, of course, and I think that the question can be put to the witness as Mr. Misetic did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The town of Obrovac was relatively undamaged by any shelling that occurred on the 4th of August, 1995. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never said that it was really damaged. I said that shells fell on several -- in several places and that this was the reason why people left. As for this video-clip, they showed specifically the places where nothing fell, no shell fell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic, if we start asking witnesses to form their opinion on the basis of what they've seen and then you take a few shots and of course journalists have a habit of showing those shots that they like most, then the reference to, on the basis what you've just seen, is not, I think, what we should pursue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Continuing further with that video, sir, first of all, do you know the Mr. Markovic who appeared on that video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you heard Mr. Markovic say that the people left at 6.00 a.m. on the 4th, on buses. Does that refresh your recollection as to when the majority of the population left Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At 6.00, it was simply impossible for them to leave, so I still remain -- I maintain my earlier statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There also appeared to be a boat in that video with the word milicija. Who or what organ of the RSK, if any, owned that boat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was -- or, rather, it was the police in Obrovac, the milicija in Obrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that video into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, I see from your body language that there are no objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number D524, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D524 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move into private session for one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session. At the same time, Mr. Misetic, we are close to the point, in a couple of minutes, where we would have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It will be very brief. I just need --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will hear this portion of the evidence and then have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would like to give instruction to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No. Just to make sure that the exhibit is not broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to have the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now is a good time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now is a good time. Then we will have a break and we resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could now show 1D37-0068, not to be broadcast to the public. If we can turn to the next page, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a statement given to the Gotovina Defence by a person who was an ARSK military police officer in Obrovac on the 4th of August, 1995. He says in his sworn statement at paragraph 2: "Prior to Operation Storm I occupied the post of military police officer in the 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac." Paragraph 4: "The military police secured the brigade command and when required intervened and participated in the combat activities." Paragraph 5: "Considering my duty, I am aware of the following locations that were used by the ARSK in Obrovac and its surrounding areas, it says: "Immediately prior to Operation Storm, the command of the 4th Light Brigade was based in the medical centre Obrovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, I believe that the Croatian word is domsdravje [phoen]. It is translated as medical centre here and I believe it is also translated as the health centre on the map that was tendered by the Prosecution this morning and marked as C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that the command of the 4th Light Brigade in the -- immediately prior to Operation Storm was located in the medical centre or the health centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. He goes on to say: "Approximately ten days prior to Operation Storm, the brigade command was relocated from the new post office building to the medical centre because it was assessed that the old command post had been discovered." Are you aware of the movement of the command of the 4th Light Brigade in the days prior to Operation Storm from the new post office building to the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know that the brigade command post was at the post office building. Secondly, I am even less aware of the fact that it was moved to the health centre. I am absolutely certain I can state with certainty that it was not ever at any point at the health centre in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He goes on to say: "Before the post office building the brigade command was based at the community centre." Do you have any knowledge of the brigade command having been once stationed in the community centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... he goes on to say: "And before that, in the hotel in Obrovac ... " Are you aware of the command at any point being stationed in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He completes that paragraph by saying: "The brigade command was secured by my MP platoon." Was it standard procedure at least when you were the commander of the 4th Light Brigade Obrovac that you would have security provided to you by a military police platoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the military police would provide security for the command post. Nothing debatable about that. However, everything else is debatable. There is even reference here to the old post office building. I don't think you could fit 40 people there. Not even if they all lay down on the floor. That is where the Territorial Defence staff used to be, two rooms about 15 square metres each, a total of 30, maybe 40 people, 30 square metres holding 40 people, I don't know, but that is probably what he had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You anticipated my next question. Then we shall move on to: "The hotel in Obrovac was used by the RSK special police platoon." We'll stop there. Was in fact the hotel being used by the special police platoon of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stand by my previous statement. The special police platoon at no point used the hotel as their accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He says: "The hotel was also used by the senior officers who were assigned in Obrovac. They were guarded by my military police unit." Were you aware of accommodations for senior ARSK officers in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know which officers he had in mind. I know that in principle, one or two officers would occasionally sleep at the hotel but it wasn't a permanent arrangement. When he says "several officers," I'm not sure who exactly he has in mind. I didn't, and I was the highest ranking member of that brigade. That's one thing that I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How many -- well, he says: "The RSK police used the police building which is currently used by the police as well. There were approximately 50 to 60 police members. I'm not certain because the number was constantly changing." What is your recollection of how many police members were typically in the police station in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he means by this. Does he mean regular police? In that case, never over 20 and this figure here is, well, you know, a bit like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He says: "At the Trio factory in Obrovac uniforms for the army and police were manufactured. I am not certain whether anything else was sewn there. We knew that our uniforms were made there." Did you in fact make uniforms for the ARSK in the Trio factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would need to tell you about the technical aspects and there is no time. I don't think there is any need. The factory could not produce any clothing. As simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the 4th of August, let me read six and seven together. "There was army in Obrovac immediately before the start of Operation Storm. I already named the units that were permanently based in Obrovac." "On 4 August, in the morning, tanks arrived in Obrovac, three tanks and three or four personnel carriers. I am not certain of the number but I know that tanks arrived that morning." Did you see, first -- I have two questions. First, did you see army personnel in Obrovac in the days leading up to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the exception of the -- a soldier here or there, but no major groups. When I see this reference to tanks, I didn't see any, and that's why I told that you the 4th Light Brigade had no tanks, it is possible that something was brought in on the 4th, on that day itself, but nothing that I saw or was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And in Obrovac, on the 4th itself, did you see tanks and personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to a map in a few minutes, but there's a bridge over the river Zrmanje in Obrovac. If the army wanted to put -- move forces into that area of the front line that you drew on the map, or rotate forces out to get over the river Zrmanje, would they have to cross over a bridge in Obrovac to get over the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and no, depending on the commander's decision because there is another crossing about 10 or 15 kilometres downstream from there. It is the bridge over the Zrmanja river, the reversible hydro power plant. So this bridge was not the only crossing that was available.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We will show the Trial Chamber the crossings over the river, but what I want to point out and ask you is, in section of the river, the only way to get across the river to the front line that you drew on the map is to go over the bring in Obrovac. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So if the army wanted to send reinforcements up to the front line, at least for that portion of the river, they would have had to go through Obrovac, over the bridge and to the front line. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should try to tackle this differently, but all right, I will say yes, just in order to make sure we don't waste any more time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to this statement and then we'll get to the bridges in a few minutes. He goes on to say: "On that day a lot of army was present in Obrovac, both permanent units, such as our unit, and the special police and army that passed through heading towards their positions. It is it difficult to say how many soldiers were present, but the town was full of them." If, in fact it turns out that the town was full of soldiers at certain points, at least, soldiers moving to the front line over the bridge in Obrovac, can you explain why it might be that you didn't see any soldiers in Obrovac on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm sorry, Your Honour. I think that assumes facts not in evidence and calls for speculation, if in fact there were a town full of soldiers and you wouldn't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to stick as close as possible to what is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can do it the long way, too, which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You've already testified, sir, that you were out several times during the day, you left the city of Obrovac, you went to go see your family, you were out on the roads. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How long -- how long did your trips out of Obrovac on the 4th take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As long as it took to cross 18 kilometres there, 18 back and about ten minutes spent with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How did you get -- it obviously depends on the means that you took to travel these 18 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So do you have a rough estimate of how much time your trips out and back took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About an hour, an hour and a half, depending.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And how many trips out of Obrovac were there on the 4th of August for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice. I went twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So it is at least three hours in the day on the 4th of August where you were present in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thereabouts. Yes, between two and three hours, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn to paragraph 8 of this statement. This witness mentions just as you mentioned in your earlier testimony there was a kitchen in Zegar. He says at the Trio factory. "The cooking was done there, meals were prepared for the entire 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac and the civilian police. The depot was also in the old school building in Zegar. It was an ammunition and fuel depot. The objects were guarded by the reserve army, the Territorial Defence?" First, did Trio have another factory in Zegar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So I may have misunderstood you before, so let's clarify again. The kitchen, was the kitchen for the military in the Trio factory in Zegar or in the old school in Zegar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Trio factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you agree with this witness that the depot was located in the old school building in Zegar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 9 he says: "There was an ammunition and equipment depot in the settlement Krupa in the school building and in private houses around the school building. Mostly artillery ammunition was kept there." Do you have any knowledge of depots in Krupa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And then this witness also mentions what we saw in Mr. Paravinja's report before the ARSK left the depot was blown up. In paragraph 10 he says: "The forward command post of the brigade was located in the factory Glinica and in the locality Caber on the Velebit. Mount Caber is a basin on the Velebit mountain. The kitchen was there." How many forward command posts did the 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac have in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about August 1995. As I said, the brigade command post was in the Glinica factory and remained there until the 24th of January, 1993 but not after. It was then moved to Caber. Therefore, this statement is true only to the extent that it mentions Caber but what it says about the Glinica factory, I know for certain that that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you know for concern -- when was the last time you visited the Glinica factory before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no need for me to visit. I hadn't visited since 1993, simply because there was no reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So from 1993 until the beginning of Operation Storm, you never physically were present at the Glinica factory. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. He goes on in paragraph 11, I'll read just read it for the record. I think I know your answer to, but you'll recall that the report of Captain Paravinja from 9 August talked about mortars, Howitzers, guns, et cetera. He says here is where they were deployed. 120-millimetre mortars, I think a mortar battery were in the village Rastovac. 105-millimetre Howitzers, I think a 105-millimetre Howitzer battery were in the village Demnjak. 122-millimetre Howitzers, I think three or four pieces were in the village Muskovci. The 130-millimetre gun was moved to various positions. I remember that it was located in Olujici, Bilisane, Muskovci and prior to Operation Storm at Krusevo in the village Sose. Let me ask you again, you have no knowledge of where this type of weaponry was deployed by the 4th Light Brigade, Obrovac, immediately preceding Operation Storm or on the 4th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, as I've explained before. I had nothing to do with the brigade. I don't know. They may have been right there. But this is the front line that I marked on the map, so, there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 12 he says: "The armoured units were in Krusevo. These were T-34 tank units which were immobile and served as guns. I do not recall their exact number. T-55 tanks were in the village Bilisane, Grande, as well as an escort personnel carrier. There were approximately six to seven of them. I am not certain of the exact number. Another T-55 was located in the village of Modrici, above Obrovac." Again, with respect to these tanks, T-55s, T-34s, personnel carriers, you have no knowledge of where any of this equipment might have been immediately preceding Operation Storm or on the 4th of August. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. But I do notice something there that is counterintuitive, if I may just tell you about that. There was a report by someone before and it was said that the T-34 tanks were blocking something over at Velebit, which means that they were moving about and here they are described as being stationary. I think this is an indication enough of fabrication. I don't believe that there this many tanks around and yet I saw none. I don't think that is plausible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's continue to the final portion. At paragraph 13: "The air defence was located in the factory Glinica, BOFORS guns, I think two pieces, and one air defence rocket Strela. In the area Berevaca above Obrovac, a Strela rocket. In the area Caber, Cabec, also Strela." You -- I think I asked you this before but let me ask you again, you would not have any information as to the location of any of these BOFORS guns or air defence rockets prior to or during Operation Storm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, consistent with our procedures here I will obviously not tender the statement and I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have read the relevant portions, especially since it will not be tendered at this moment. You called it a sworn statement. I see that it is given and attested by a notary public that a statement was given but I do not see any oath taken anywhere. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. I may not have used the term properly. If we flip to the signature page I think there's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've read the signature page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't have it in front of me, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's have a look at it. At least I have looked at the translation and we have the certification of the notary public and even what he charged for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can flip up, I'm actually interested in the one above. You're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially since it is not in evidence, I think it is good to have it precisely on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just one point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that the procedure was to mark it for identification but not tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It depends on whether there were ever -- whether this person will ever be called as a witness because under those circumstances we could seek attestations, further attestations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Obviously if there is an Defence case we intend to call him. However in light of the Gojanovic documents which ultimately the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We don't want to have them on the list --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in certain circumstances so as soon as a witness is expected to testify then we keep them on the MFI list and if not, then of course at a later stage they can be reintroduced on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Whether you wish to MFI them or -- it doesn't matter to me, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that for the time being this would -- Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could now turn to 1D37-0080, please. If we could start with page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is -- if we could also get the English. I don't know if we can do both. Now, Witness, in light of the fact that you do not know or have any information about the location of specific types of weaponry, you may not be able to identify many of the locations here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And this is for the benefit of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: However you mentioned Zegar, which is at number 11, and can you confirm that that is in fact the location where the kitchen and arms depot was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At number 10, that is where Krupa is located, but I believe your testimony is you were unaware of any depots in Krupa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And let us turn the page. Okay. This is now the map of the bridges along the river Zrmanje. And you had anticipated some of what I wanted to talk to you about. The river Zrmanje divides the north-west portion of what was then the Republika Srpska Krajina from Knin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I quite understand. Can you repeat that one for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The river Zrmanje is a line that divides the north, north-west from where Knin is located and the southern part of the Sector South or so-called Republika Srpska Krajina, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in a manner of speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now to cross that river, there were four crossing points, correct? Actually, yeah, four crossing points and those crossing points were the bridge in Obrovac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe you started to mention this earlier in your testimony the bridge at the power plant Obrovac-Muskovci. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There is an bridge in Krupa. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bring in Krupa has nothing to do with the Zrmanje river. It is a bridge on the Krupa river.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are those two rivers connected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The Krupa flows into the Zrmanje but lower down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if you look on this map, the bridge at Kastel Zegarski, can you tell us what river that crosses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Zrmanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if those bridges had been blown up by artillery, how would one have gotten from Knin, let's say, to the front line, where you draw it on the map for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Zrmanje river is above the bridge on Kastel Zegarski, which means upstream about two and a half to three kilometres and it is possible to cross the Zrmanje by just wading through the water because it is it not very deep. In Ervenik the river ends. There is no water flow in the summer. One could also come to Knin from a different direction from Knin-Gracac on the road, by the road. So it was possible to reach this place even without the bridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It would have been considerably more difficult to get from Knin to the front line where you drew it on the map if those bridges were not in place, than simply to go straight to Obrovac or to Muskovci, cross the bridge and get to the front line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends on where the troops that needed to reach the front line were, so the road from -- via Gracac to Obrovac is not any longer than the road via Ervenik and Zegari, if that's what you're asking, if that is the purpose of your question. In fact, I think I understand what your question is aiming at but this is all can I answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to figure out what the aim of Mr. Misetic's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's say they wanted to rotate troops from Benkovac to the front line. If the bridge there Obrovac were destroyed how would troops go from Benkovac to the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was expecting this question. It was possible to cross the Zrmanje river on foot, beyond the bridge in Kasatel Zegarski and it was also possible to cross it on the white waters where, in the summer, you can cross it. There is no impediment there to just cross it by walking and this is even closer than the Kastel bring or the Muskovci bridge. So one could cross the river over these two waterfalls, if you want to call them, or just white waters there just by Muskovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, was the bridge ever destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It wasn't destroyed, no, that's a good point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It still could be used. What is the use of saying if the bridge would be there, what would be -- of course apart from taking another bridge, isn't it true that if a bridge is not to be used anymore that you would adapt all kind of operational -- you might relocate troops for that purpose. I mean what is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have testimony, well, I prefer not to do this -- he probably speaks English, but -- He is answering my questions pretty quickly before the translation's done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR.  MISETIC
utterances.text: -- so I'm not sure he doesn't. But the point being the testimony of the witness is there were no military targets and no reason to shell Obrovac and that's -- in the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So I think the witness is fully aware that shelling the bridge in Obrovac, if nothing else, would impede the RSK army in light of the configuration of the territory, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Your Honour, I would ask that this PowerPoint be marked and I tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There's two points, Your Honour. First of all only two of these pages were shown to the witness and not the other ones, so I guess just want to know what the foundation of the other ones is. And the second point is on the previous page, what's shown as a bunch of locations have been identified and I'm just wondering if there is any other information on the underlying information more than the report that was shown in the statement of the witness and if there is so that we know where these circles on the map and numbers come from. Barring that, there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, it is clear that the witness could identify only one or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us who else invented what was on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is prepared by our team, Your Honour. It's based on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is whatever the witness could not confirm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- remains there not as anything from a source which this Chamber could rely on but is just what the understanding of the Defence is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's right. And with respect to the prior pages, some of the prior pages some of them are general maps. There is a section in there about the Maslenica operation in 1993 which I now don't feel the need to go through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So if just we can put on there that we have no intention at this point to use those, just the two that were shown, one of which is limited to what this witness was able to identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a possibility to recreate them in such a way --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that we are not confused by any information about what was where if it is not adduced in evidence in the usual way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you wish, I can just print out just these two pages and admit them as the exhibit, replace the one that is there now in e-court with the one that's shortened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. Therefore you don't have to print it out but to manipulate what now comes into e-court. I suggest that we ask provisionally for a number to Mr. Registrar, mark it for identification that you upload the final versions which can create no confusion as far as the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Chamber is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number D525 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D525 is awaiting to be replaced by another version. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My final set of questions, sir, is you were -- the Prosecution has told the Defence that they were able to contact you through Mr. Sovo Strboc and his organisation Veritas. Can you tell us how you were made aware that the Prosecution wished to speak to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the answer is contained in your question, in other words, through Mr. Strboc.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Strboc called you up and said that the Office of the Prosecutor wished to speak to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And what did he tell you they wished to speak to you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have a lengthy conversation with Mr. Strboc, but in general he said that they wanted to talk to me about these events relating to the 4th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And specifically did he tell that you the Office of the Prosecutor wished to speak to you about shelling in Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Only about the events and the knowledge that I had, but nobody mentioned any specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And finally my last question is, how well do you know Mr. Strboc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depends what you mean by that. I knew him from way back when we were in school together in Zadar. It wasn't a very close relationship, and I only met him again in 1992 or 1993 in Benkovac. So I -- I have known him for many years, but we didn't have all that many encounters. So, in that sense, I have known him for a brief time. I know him from the home in Zadar, but after that, I didn't meet him up until 1992 or 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for coming to testify, Mr. Dupud.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Misetic, I've got a question for you. All the distances indicated on the bridges map are distances by road, I take it, and not as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it is as the crow flies, but let me confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You're right. Let me get the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the squares on a map depict, these size of maps, square kilometres. If that would be the case, then certainly it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will have the answer to you by the time we finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, the witness -- do you know these distances you find on that map, are these distances as the crow flies or distances if you take the shortest route by road? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have to look at the scale of the map and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I notice that we didn't put the scale on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is an scale on but of course I take it has been enlarged. It says scale 1:60.000, but as soon as you start enlarging, then scale doesn't help anymore unless the scale is there set out in kilometres because you enlarge and reduce that together with the map but that's not what we find here from what I see. We -- we'll wait for your final answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Nothing from us, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dupud, in these proceedings I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Markac, and, please -- I will have a few questions for you, so pleas answer to the best of your abilities. I do have a request for you, because we speak the same language, we need to pause between question and answer so that our words can be interpreted. Mr. Dupud, you mentioned that you are an engineer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell us what is your formal education, your formal background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The higher textile school in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you undergo any military training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The reserve officers' school and some courses, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You were a reserve officer in the JNA. What was your rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a major.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: And what was your rank in the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had the same rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar please pull up Exhibit P551. That's a map that we saw during the questions that the Prosecutor had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While we wait for the map to come up, let me just say that this is a map where you've marked certain positions and what I would like to ask you about is the front line. As I said, after 1993, in other words, after Operation Maslenica. While we're waiting for the map to come up, tell us, did the front line, after the Maslenica operation in 1993 up until August 1995, did the front line change?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Just a few more minutes, now we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, I have a hard copy of the witness if that can make it easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, in fact, I would like to blow up the upper portion of the chart because I think it would be more visible if we blow it up. Okay, that's it. I think that suffice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dupud, in the upper part of the map where we can see the front line you notice that left of the last dot to the west of the last dot, we can see Tulove Grede. Can you remember at the time we are discussing here, which is 1993, and since you mentioned that there was no change in the front line up until August 1995, who -- or which was the neighbouring unit of the Obrovac brigade holding this position? I mean the neighbour to the north on the other side of the Velebit mountain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military neighbour was the Gracac Brigade, I think. I think it was a brigade of the 15th Corps. But in any case, from Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you know the commander of that brigade, Mr. Jovan Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many men the brigade had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know where its command post was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I'm not sure, but I think it was in Gracac somewhere, to the west. I'm not sure. I can't really reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I suppose you don't know how many men it numbered or what kind of weapons it had, the Gracac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Today during your evidence, and I'm referring to page 85, line 2, you said that there were T-34 tanks on the Velebit mountain. Do you know exactly where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know that they were on Mount Velebit and now I am maintaining that they weren't there. Because the Velebit area is not passable for a tank. So I did not say that there were tanks up there. Somebody else said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You mentioned in your -- during your evidence, Mr. Dupud, you mentioned the police and approximately how many men they had. What was the role of the police within the defence framework, the defence of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police conducted the normal tasks that it did in peacetime, so it -- the regular police forces did not have any role in the defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that the police did not contribute on the forward front line -- defence lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely, that is what I'm claiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: There was also talk about the evacuation of civilians. I wouldn't want to expand on that. Perhaps just a question or two. After you were demobilised you were a manager of a factory. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: How many people did the factory employ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, there were 975 employees. In 1993, it operated at a lower capacity because in 1991 and 1992 it was not operational, and there were about 120 employees, most of them women. Perhaps one or two mechanics but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Was there an evacuation plan for the factory employees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that in the event of a threat or a dangerous situation there was no plan for evacuation for the factory workers to bring them to safety?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: You mean there was no plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, there was no plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you left Obrovac around midnight and then that you left Zegari and that you were going on -- on the road to -- to Gracac when you left. Did you enter Gracac itself, the town of Gracac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: If I recall your words correctly you said that from Gracac you headed for Srb. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Stikade is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is a town on the road between Gracac and Gospic, some seven kilometres to the west of Gracac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not go through Stikada town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no need for that, because it is not on the road to Srb. You don't have to go through it if you want to go to Srb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Tell me then, how is it that you said that in Gracac and in Stikada at the time when you went through them there were no Croatian troops when you never went into Gracac or Stikada?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because on the Obrovac-Gracac road, the police was positioned there, and they stopped me and they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So, in other words, your evidence is that you did not see this for yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Did you observe the withdrawal of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have one point of clarification that just arose, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Dupud, you were shown a statement from another witness about where the forward command post may be located. There was the hotel, the post office and the Glinica factory and the location in the Velebit. So I'm just a little confused can you clarify for me. Until 1993 when you were the commander of the 4th Light Brigade, how many forward command posts were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to clarify the question because it doesn't accurately characterize what the statement says. There is a distinction between the command location and a forward command post and I believe the witness statement says there were two forward command posts but multiple command headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, are you able to include this in your question, this --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Until 1993 when you were the commander of the 4th Light Brigade, how many forward command posts were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A forward command post is only in use or becomes operational once combat begins, and by -- until 1993, the 20th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure of the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- of January 1993, the command post was where it was marked on the map. After this, the other command post was formed on the Velebit mountain, and it was a single forward command post, because there was no need to have another forward command post. In other words, there was just this one forward command post, except if there is something that I wasn't aware of. Or, rather, I claim that there was only this one command post on the Velebit mountain and no others. And, of course, I also clarified about Zegar. In addition to the ammunitions depot there and the kitchen or the mess hall, there was also an administration building or offices for the brigade and these administrative services do not mean that there was a brigade command there. The brigade command was up on the Velebit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Other than the forward command posts, were there any other command locations of the 4th Light Brigade in Obrovac when you were commander of the 4th Light Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Gwaunza has one question for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Just one question. Going back to your statement, paragraph 5 -- sorry. If I could just ask one question, and that goes back to your statement, paragraph 5, where you talked about personally knowing of seven or eight people who stayed behind and they were killed. Did you ever get to know how they were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that this was indirect knowledge. I learned of this from the families of these people. And, of course, at the very start when that happened, so that I do not have any personal knowledge as to how this came about, how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Question of the Bench has not triggered any need for further questions. Then, Mr. Dupud, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to testify, for having answered all the questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, Mr. Hedaraly, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness, let me first ask you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we are at a quarter to 2.00. Nevertheless, if we would start for only five to ten minutes with the next witness, then we might be better to able to know where we stand, also for the coming days. It might not come as a surprise that before this Chamber could decide on the admission of 92 ter statements that, first of all, one of the requirements, of course, would be the attestation and since this might become a matter of which we would prefer to know about at this moment rather than by surprise tomorrow morning, the Chamber is seeking, as a matter of fact, another ten minutes to see whether we can come to a point where at least we have some information which is of high relevance for the coming days. Would there be any objection by the Defence to -- that is to set one step then, of course -- Good afternoon, Ms. Mahindaratne. Yes. No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. I'm not quite sure how we wish to proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, to call the witness perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I have no objection to staying later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, of course, then I have to sort out my problems with the next Chamber who is schedule for this courtroom. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the next witness there is no request for protective measures as far as I understand. You are the one who takes the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for very practical purposes, have you communicated these days with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We haven't had any kind of communication whatsoever. We attempted to proof the witness in Zagreb but the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That answers already my question. Then are you ready to call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now before you give his name because out of an abundance of caution the Chamber would like to go into private session for a minute to find out, especially since there has been no communication with you, whether the witness would want to seek any protective measures. Just to find out whether there's any wish in that respect. So, therefore, the witness is to be brought into the courtroom; at the same time, we turn into private session. That means that all protective measures, as we could envisage are temporarily in place.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I think that then that also the curtain could be -- yes, if you ... Mr. Hedaraly, you'll get some instruction on how to move the curtains. Yes, could I, first of all, ask you to refrain from having eye contact with all kind of people, the ones who are addressing you at this moment, it's me and then after that the party who will examine you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please stand and under the rules you are required to make a solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for the eye contact previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, are you ready to -- and I don't know whether you were already in the courtroom when I explained that we would make a short start.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. President I learned of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Janic, you will first be examined by Ms. Mahindaratne who is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Janic. Can you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Zdravko Janic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: I am a commander of the special police with the Ministry of Interior, of Croatia, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: On 13th and 14th of January, 2004, were you interviewed by investigators attached to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?
