utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And was that interview conducted with an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When the investigators questioned you, did you answer those questions truthfully?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And were those answers recorded in a statement form, type-written?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes. At least as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at the completion of the interview, the conclusion, was that statement read back to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did you sign that statement?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: I don't quite remember. I think so, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call for document number 5217, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janic, you will see a document on your screen right in front of you. And if you could take a look at that document and identify it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if we could go through each page so that Mr. Janic could identify his signature on each page, at the bottom of each page, going right up to the signature page. Mr. Janic, do you note your signature at the bottom of each of these pages? I think we don't see the bottom. Your signature is in the English copy, Mr. Janic.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Right now I can't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. Now you could see it.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, these are initials, not a full signature. The full signature was on the last page alone. The remaining pages were initialed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If we could go to the last page if you could just ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your full signature?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janic, are you familiar with the content today, or do you need to read this document because I'm going to be asking you if the contents are true to the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: I remember the substance of my statement. I studied it. There are perhaps a number of things that were perhaps not quite translated appropriately, but this does not, at any point, distort the meaning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are you able to answer my question, then, when I ask you if the contents of this statement are true to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if the questions that were asked of you by the investigators were asked today in court, would you respond in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would, the same way. Maybe not each of the letters I spoke were translated accurately, as I was speaking, but the gist is still there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can we just, first, ask you at what stage did you realise or note that there were inaccuracies in the interpretation or translation? When did you realise that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: As I was preparing for my evidence here. These are not major inaccuracy, but I can't say I haven't noticed a number of inaccuracies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let be very practical, Ms. Mahindaratne. When you prepared for your testimony today, did you have the B/C/S version available to you of your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... English available.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think, Ms. Mahindaratne, I think the wisest thing to do is, because we have to stop anyhow very soon, to ask the witness to check exactly where the issues and minor inaccuracies are and then to tell us about it tomorrow. Would you be willing to tell us -- I don't know how many there are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Ms. Mahindaratne, of course, this seems -- I would not have been surprised if you would have started with the other statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could also -- I note there is a decision pending on the video recorded interview. Subject to that, perhaps we take the opportunity to ask the witness that tonight he also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can tell you already that the -- to the extent the Prosecution has sought exclusion under Rule 95 that that request is denied and that the decision will be filed this afternoon. That's just exclusion on the basis of 95. Yes? Also for your information. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne, and let's try to get -- see whether we can finish in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, were you also interviewed in 2005 in Zagreb field office?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer. The interpreter could not hear his answer.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, I had -- I was in the status of suspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And during that interview -- no. Was that interview conducted via an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And during that interview, were you represented by your counsel?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you were asked questions by the investigators, did you respond truthfully?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the point where we may wish to have him get advice of counsel before he answers the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether he needs advice of counsel. But Mr. Janic, if by answering any question to Ms. Mahindaratne you would expose yourself to further investigation or prosecution, either on the basis of what is asked, the content, or if you would consider that answering that question truthfully might reveal that at any earlier stage you committed an offence, whatever that offence would be, whether it would be offences in 1995 or at any later stage, then you can ask the Chamber not to be obliged to answer such a question. Nevertheless, the Chamber, under certain conditions, has the power to force you to at least to oblige you to, nevertheless, answer the question. If it comes to that, I will further explain the matter to you. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Janic, my question, I do not know if you responded to that -- yes. When you were asked questions by members of the Office of the Prosecutor, did you answer those questions truthfully?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: What are you referring to? I -- I'm not sure I understood. Which questioning do you mean? As a witness, in 1994; or as a suspect in 2005?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: As a suspect in 2005.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Well, as my counsel advised me, that my statement, as a suspect, cannot be used in these proceedings. I was advised, in other words, I was told, that only my statement given as a witness in 2004 can be used in these proceedings. I don't know if I'm right about this and I would appreciate the Presiding Judge advising me thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that advice was given to you at the time, then, of course, we'd have to distinguish between certain matters. That is, whether it could be used against you yourself if you would ever have been indicted, which I do understand is not the case; and if your counsel, at that time, would have said that under no circumstances your statement could be used, then that advice was not accurate. But -- so, therefore, that statement, under certain circumstances, can be used. Whether it will be used is still a matter to be seen. But at this moment we are still at the point where Ms. Mahindaratne asked you whether you answered the questions truthfully. Could you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And were those -- was that interview video recorded?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At the conclusion of your interview, was your attorney handed over three copies of the video tapes?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to review those video tapes since then, that's recently, or the transcripts thereof?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO JANIC
utterances.text: No. I do have the video tapes in my possession, but because the counsel told me then that my suspect interview could not be used in these proceedings, I did not consider it necessary to prepare and review those video tapes. I prepared exclusively by reading my witness statement from 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is why I wanted to finish today. Perhaps we could ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have, of course, a bit of a different situation here since there's a video recording available. We have, as a matter of fact, two questions mainly remain not whether the statement as such reflects what the witness said because unless there's any suspicion of forgery with the tapes, that question could be verified by the Chamber itself. We now have an answer of the witness to the question whether he truthfully answered the -- that he truthfully answered the questions that were put to him at that time. The one, then, remaining question would be, Mr. Janic, whether you would give the same answers if the same questions would be put to you in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest, Ms. Mahindaratne, that we give an opportunity to this witness also and even the technical facilities, to review the video or the written statements, so that if there are any corrections to be made, that they could be made. At the same time, I take it that you want to tender both statements under 92 ter, Rule 92 ter and we have heard already that there are objections by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President and with regard to the statement there were no objections from the Defence and I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This statement, not the interview which, of course, then would also be a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There we stand at this moment. I -- of course the Chamber would like to know whether the attestation would be given as required because if there is no attestation, then, of course, matters are quite different. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, we are now, of course, at a different stage; that is, a stage where the documents have been tendered. Until now, the submissions by the parties were in a different procedural stage. Now, of course, the question is how to proceed. May I take it that there still are objections against admission for the same reasons as you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything that you would like to add to those reasons?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not -- and then, of course, I'm looking at the clock. I've stolen already 25 minutes, so we really have to conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Then I would prefer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way of informing Mr. Tieger and the bench perhaps because we are -- of course, we are running out of time. If you want to continue tomorrow morning, to put it briefly on paper whether any additional arguments and if it could not be filed, then at least to send already a courtesy copy and of course the shorter you take it, the quicker it goes. Of course if you need a bit more time, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't anticipate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You must have given some thought already to the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And if we have anything we will certainly e-mail it around this evening. We just wanted to note that it appears that there were some issues that have been raised concerning some of the technical matters regarding this witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In other words, all of these technical issues with respect to this witness's 92 ter statement that we've gone through now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These, of course, are the questions that have to be put to the witness if a party is seeking to have the 92 ter statements admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, we were unaware -- I was unaware that the Prosecution had not had an opportunity to communicate with -- with the witness prior to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that, of course, created a bit of a different situation because it was uncertain what would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. I'm not just saying that if there had been a communication with the Chamber on that, we were not copied on that. So we've been unaware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is -- let me be, then, very candid on that. One of our legal officers has informed the Chamber that, as far as he knew, that there had been no -- no -- as you say, no proofing session and that the witness had not communicated. That's all the information the Chamber received.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if could I add. In fact, we made it clear in the application for the subpoena that as to what really occurred when we attempted to proof the witness, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, of course, is not an answer as to what happened the last two days but it might not have come as a surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I was unaware. That's fine, Your Honour. I just wanted to say that for that reason I do need a couple of hours tonight and if we have anything at all, I will e-mail it around to everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just -- since the witness has confirmed the statement, that is, not the recording, but with regard to the -- could I move admission of the statement into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the statement and the interview?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At this stage since this is an issue about it, the interview we could deal with tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, as a matter of fact whether we decide is another matter but, of course, it would be good to know whether it is tendered and I understood that you want to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then, both are tendered and then Mr. Registrar could you please assign provisional numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first document was 65 ter 05217 and that becomes Exhibit number P552, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the other one was?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the other document will be marked for identification as Exhibit number P553.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and they keep the status of marked for identification. Mr. Janic, at this moment, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony you are about to give, because there's not much yet that you have given, and we adjourn for the day. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, the 9th of July, at 9.00, in this Courtroom II. I apologise, not only for the other Chamber, I have not sought your consent to continue but it was really very urgent to have this part done. I apologise, for interpreters, for not having consulting them and for the transcriber and, of course, all others who are assisting us in this courtroom, and I will personally see that I'll take care that you get at least the rest you deserve. Again, apologies, and I will not do it again. We stand adjourned until tomorrow.
